candidates.why_relevant: Single regulator-maintained hub of five parallel index pages, each mapping a licensed entity type to the exact URL on that entity's own website where its statutory disclosures (Vyhláška 163/2014 Sb., CRR Part Eight) live. This is the authoritative seed list for the whole cell: it yielded all 5 building societies, 6 credit unions, 9 pension companies, 35 investment firms and 8 investment companies with deep-links, and it is refreshed by ČNB as entities rename or migrate domains. Snowballing from here removes the need to guess corporate websites.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů (JERRS) + otevřená data / WS JERRS
candidates.why_relevant: Legally binding register of every licensed entity in scope of this cell — stavební spořitelny (licensed as banks), spořitelní a úvěrní družstva, penzijní společnosti and their účastnické/transformované/důchodové fondy, and obchodníci s cennými papíry. Gives IČO, legal name history, licence scope and licence dates, which is what makes entity-level annual reports findable in the commercial register and lets us detect new licences, withdrawals and renames. ČNB also exposes machine-readable open data and WS JERRS web services (since 1.7.2019), so this can be polled deterministically rather than scraped.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Consume WS JERRS web services or the ČNB open-data exports on a monthly schedule; maintain an IČO-keyed entity master table to join to commercial-register filings and to each entity's own disclosure page.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Czech-language search on JERRS + fetch of ČNB 'Seznamy a evidence' hub

candidates.source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (Ministerstvo spravedlnosti ČR) + Justice open data
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory filing archive: every stavební spořitelna, spořitelní družstvo, penzijní společnost and obchodník s cennými papíry must file its účetní závěrka, výroční zpráva and auditor's report into the Sbírka listin. This is the fallback of record whenever an entity's own website hides, moves or prunes its annual reports (and the only reliable route for the smaller credit unions, which publish irregularly). dataor.justice.cz offers bulk open data for the register itself, enabling IČO-driven automated retrieval.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Resolve each in-scope entity to an IČO via JERRS/ARES, then poll its Sbírka listin document list annually (Apr–Aug filing window) and download new výroční zpráva / účetní závěrka PDFs; use dataor.justice.cz bulk data for register metadata.

queries_used: justice.cz sbírka listin veřejný rejstřík výroční zpráva účetní závěrka vyhledávání

candidates.why_relevant: Annual supervisory report that counts and characterises the exact populations in this cell — banks including building societies, spořitelní a úvěrní družstva, pension companies and their funds, investment firms — and records licence grants, withdrawals, mergers and enforcement. It is the single best instrument for detecting that an entity in the cell has stopped existing or changed group affiliation, and for validating the completeness of any entity list assembled from disclosure indexes. Long PDF back-series (at least 2008 onward) enables consistent historical entity counts.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual pull of the new dnft_{YYYY}_cz.pdf from the ČNB gallery path; parse entity-count tables and licensing sections into the entity master.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Czech-language search returning the ČNB report gallery PDFs directly

candidates.source_name: Garanční systém finančního trhu (Fond pojištění vkladů, Fond pro řešení krize)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory deposit-guarantee and resolution-funding body to which every CZ-headquartered bank, building society and credit union must contribute by law. Its participant lists and contribution data provide an independent, exhaustive census of exactly the deposit-taking half of this cell, and its disclosures reveal failures and payouts (historically the main event risk for credit unions). It also issues bonds with base prospectuses, adding a further disclosure stream.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual crawl of the povinně zveřejňované informace section for the annual report and participant list; monitor news items for payout events affecting cell entities.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Czech-language search on deposit insurance covering credit unions and building societies

candidates.source_name: AKAT ČR – Asociace pro kapitálový trh: statistiky správců aktiv a tiskové zprávy
candidates.why_relevant: Trade body covering investment companies, asset managers, obchodníci s cennými papíry and banks operating on the CZ capital market — i.e. the investment-firm portion of this cell. Publishes quarterly aggregate AUM statistics (e.g. CZK 3.16tn entrusted to asset managers at 31.12.2024) broken down by manager and product type, providing the sector denominator that individual investment-firm annual reports lack. Press-release PDFs are often mirrored by member firms, giving alternate retrieval paths when the association site is awkward.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly scrape of the statistics/press-release sections; fall back to member-firm mirrors of the same TZ PDFs when the primary listing is unavailable.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Czech-language search for the capital-market association's asset-manager statistics
queries_used: AKAT ČR Asociace pro kapitálový trh statistiky správci aktiv tiskové zprávy

candidates.source_name: Stavebky.cz a Hypoindex.cz – odborný tisk ke stavebnímu spoření
candidates.why_relevant: Czech specialist trade press covering the building-society segment continuously, including annual 'jak si vedly stavební spořitelny' reviews, rate and tariff comparisons across all five societies, and coverage of distribution changes. Valuable as an early-warning and dating layer: rate moves, product withdrawals and branch/advisor changes appear here weeks or months before they are formalised in a výroční zpráva, and articles frequently cite the underlying entity documents, acting as a pointer.
candidates.legal_status: copyrighted editorial content — link and summarise, do not republish
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/HTML monitoring of both sites with entity-name keyword filters; store headline + date + link and follow through to any primary document cited.
candidates.discovered_via_method: Czech-language seed query results; recurring across multiple searches

negative_findings.description: English-language searching was run in parallel with Czech throughout ('Czech building society annual report subsidiary Erste KBC Societe Generale Raiffeisen disclosure', 'Czech credit union cooperative savings annual report disclosure Pillar 3') and returned almost nothing usable at entity level for this cell.
negative_findings.result_summary: English queries returned parent-group material (KBC Group annual reports, the 2019 KBC/ČSOB buyout of BSH's 45% ČMSS stake) and generic EBA/Basel Pillar 3 documents, but no CZ non-bank subsidiary disclosure pages. Of the five building societies, only Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna (confirmed bilingual PDFs 2020–2025) and MONETA Stavební Spořitelna (bilingual IR pages) publish English. Buřinka's annual-report index is Czech-only; ČNB's disclosure indexes were reached only via Czech URLs. No English-language disclosure page was found for any credit union or pension company.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collector built on English queries would miss roughly the entire cell. Retrieval must be Czech-first, and downstream extraction must handle Czech financial terminology (výroční zpráva, účetní závěrka, účastnický fond, transformovaný fond, povinně uveřejňované informace) rather than expecting English equivalents.

negative_findings.description: The URL ČNB's official bank-disclosure index still gives for ČSOB Stavební spořitelna is https://www.cmss.cz/informace-dle-vyhlasky-cnb, from the pre-rebrand Českomoravská stavební spořitelna era.
negative_findings.result_summary: One fetch of that URL returned ECONNREFUSED 193.245.72.249:443. A targeted Czech search recovered a live replacement at csobstavebni.cz with both /vyrocni-zpravy and /informace-dle-vyhlasky-cnb. Recorded as a stale-domain hypothesis, not a dead source — the entity is plainly active.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Even the authoritative regulator index carries lagging URLs after rebrands. A collector must treat an index entry failure as a rename signal and re-resolve the entity by name/IČO rather than marking it dead, or it will silently lose the largest building society in the market.

negative_findings.description: https://www.modrapyramida.cz/dokumenty could not be fetched by the strict-TLS fetcher.
negative_findings.result_summary: Error: 'Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames: Host: www.modrapyramida.cz is not in the cert's altnames: DNS:www.kb.cz, DNS:kb.cz'. Hypothesis: the domain is now served from Komerční banka infrastructure as part of the ongoing absorption of Modrá pyramida into KB, so content is live but the certificate does not cover the legacy hostname.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most strategically loaded entity in the cell (branch conversion to KB poradenská místa, advisor absorption, servicing moved to KB+) and it is exactly the one a naive fetcher drops. Collection needs a browser-grade client, plus kb.cz and Sbírka listin as parallel routes.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for Investiční společnost České spořitelny's mandatory disclosures as a candidate bank-group investment firm.
negative_findings.result_summary: ISČS ceased to exist as a Czech legal entity: Erste Asset Management GmbH became sole shareholder in 2009 and a cross-border merger in 2015 absorbed ISČS into Erste Asset Management GmbH, with services now offered through 'Erste Asset Management GmbH, pobočka Česká republika' (IČO 04107128, registered at the Municipal Court in Prague). A branch files differently from a Czech joint-stock company, so there is no equivalent standalone CZ statutory annual report.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: One of the largest bank-group asset managers in CZ has no entity-level Czech annual report to sweep. Coverage of the Erste/ČS asset-management side must instead come from Erste AM group disclosures, REICO (the ČS-group real-estate investment company, which does remain a Czech entity), and AKAT aggregates — otherwise the cell's investment-firm coverage looks complete when it is not.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for the Asociace družstevních záložen (ADZ), the credit-union trade body, expecting an association counterpart to AČSS and APS ČR.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only third-party directory profiles were returned (uspory.cz, penize.cz, fintimes.cz, druzstevni-inkubator.cz). Background surfaced: ADZ founded 2001 by WPB Capital, Prague Credit Union and DZ NOVA; roughly five of the credit unions described as members. No official ADZ domain appeared in results, and no association statistics comparable to AČSS or APS ČR were located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The credit-union segment has no usable association-level aggregator. Sector totals for družstevní záložny must come from ČNB ARAD and the supervision report, and entity detail must be assembled union by union — a materially more expensive collection pattern than for building societies or pension companies.

negative_findings.description: Sought a consolidated, machine-readable source of branch counts, advisor headcount or self-service/ATM estate for the non-bank licensed entities in this cell.
negative_findings.result_summary: No such registry or dataset was found in Czech or English. Channel facts surfaced only as narrative: KB press releases dating the conversion of ~190 Modrá pyramida branches to KB advisory points and the move of ~500 advisors into KB's network, and Patria Finance's own description of developing its trading applications. Nothing equivalent exists as a periodic structured feed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's core value — entity-level channel and technology signal — must be extracted from prose in annual reports and press releases rather than read off a table. Collection design should assume text extraction plus manual review, and should prioritise the narrative sections of výroční zprávy over the financial statements.

coverage_gaps.description: Four of the nine ČNB-listed pension companies — Allianz, UNIQA, Conseq and Rentea penzijní společnost — were captured only via the ČNB index entry and were not individually profiled or fetched in this pass. Rentea in particular is a newer entrant whose distribution model has not been characterised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch each of the four disclosure URLs from the ČNB pension index, confirm the annual-report location and format, and add them as candidates so the third-pillar entity set is complete before any market-share reasoning is attempted.

coverage_gaps.description: The ČNB investiční společnosti index as fetched returned only eight entities and included 'AXA investiční společnost a.s.', a name superseded by the UNIQA rebrand, while omitting REICO investiční společnost České spořitelny, which other sources show still exists. The list is therefore either partially stale or truncated in retrieval, so the bank-group investment-company population cannot be treated as settled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Rebuild the investment-company and investment-firm population from JERRS / WS JERRS rather than from the HTML disclosure indexes, and reconcile the two lists; add REICO and any other ČS/KB/UniCredit/Raiffeisen-group managers found.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell definition frames credit unions as sitting 'inside the same banking groups' as the other entity types. Nothing found supports this for CZ: all six ČNB-indexed spořitelní družstva (Artesa, Citfin, České spořitelní družstvo, NEY, Peněžní dům, Podnikatelská družstevní záložna) appear to be standalone cooperatives, not bank-group subsidiaries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat CZ credit unions as an independent comparator segment rather than a window into banking-group strategy, and reallocate expected analytical weight toward building societies, pension companies and in-group investment firms, which genuinely are group subsidiaries.

coverage_gaps.description: No check was made of whether historical annual-report PDFs remain retrievable after site migrations. Two migrations are already visible in this cell (ČMSS to csobstavebni.cz, burinka.cz to burinka.csas.cz) and a third is in progress (modrapyramida.cz to KB infrastructure), each of which typically prunes older documents.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Back-fill and mirror the full available archives now — Buřinka's 2000–2025 series and Raiffeisen's 2020–2025 bilingual set are the priorities — and record Wayback Machine snapshots for the migrating domains before older files disappear.

coverage_gaps.description: Parent-group reporting that describes these CZ subsidiaries — KBC/ČSOB, Erste Group/Česká spořitelna, Société Générale-lineage KB, Raiffeisen Bank International, Generali CEE — was touched only incidentally through KBC group annual reports surfaced in English search, and not systematically mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm with the run coordinator whether parent-group IR belongs to another coverage cell; if not, add the five group IR sites as indirect sources, since group reports date CZ subsidiary restructurings and IT programmes that the local entity report describes only after the fact.

coverage_gaps.description: Several candidate URLs were carried forward from the ČNB indexes without an independent fetch — notably ČSOB Asset Management, Generali Investments CEE, Amundi CZ, NEY, Peněžní dům, Podnikatelská družstevní záložna and České spořitelní družstvo. Their document depth, formats and update cadence are therefore unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over every candidate URL and example URL in this slice, and treat any 403 or timeout as bot defence to be retried with a browser-grade client rather than as evidence the source is dead.

brief: The Czech non-bank licensed segment is unusually well mapped by its own regulator: ČNB maintains five parallel 'přehled odkazů' index pages that deep-link each licensed entity to its own statutory disclosure page, and between them they define this cell's entire universe — 5 building societies (ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida, MONETA, Raiffeisen, Buřinka), 6 credit unions, 9 pension companies, 8 investment companies and 35 investment firms — with JERRS and the Sbírka listin as authoritative backstops. Disclosure quality is highly uneven: Raiffeisen and MONETA publish bilingual annual reports on disciplined schedules and Artesa publishes parseable quarterly XLSX, while the smaller credit unions and several bank-group managers require commercial-register retrieval, and English-language coverage is close to absent outside those two building societies. The cell's distinctive payoff is already visible — Modrá pyramida's ~190 branches converting to KB advisory points with ~500 advisors absorbed and servicing migrating to KB+, and Patria Finance describing its own trading-platform development — none of which is broken out in the parent groups' consolidated reports. The main risks to collection are stale regulator links after rebrands (cmss.cz), TLS/host mismatches on entities mid-integration (modrapyramida.cz), and archive loss during the several site migrations now under way.
